# Introduction

This is a fun project for me. It's allowing me to take pieces I learned from risk communication and perception, specifically cognitive maps, and combine them with what I learned from stochastic compartment modeling. I also had a professor, back in the day, say, "We all use models. Epidemiologists write them down". And so here I am putting my intuition into a mathematical model to describe my experience with why prevailing attitudes change.

A good example of things changing... I remember when Taylor Swift first hit the scene. She was different and not everyone liked her music. Fast forward to today, she's a hit across the board. Even I like her!!

So, how does my intuition process her rise to stardom? Take a look below.

# My compartment model output

```{r, include = TRUE, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 7}
library(easypackages)

libraries(
  c(
    "ggplot2", 
    "tidyr", 
    "tidyverse", 
    "ggpubr", 
    "readxl", 
    "janitor"
  )
)

sim = read.csv("Pass001_simulations2_df.csv")

sim2 = 
  sim %>% 
  mutate(
    susceptible = S,
    fence = L,
    spreaders = I + C, 
    non_spreaders = S + R + W
  ) 

ggplot(
  sim2
) + 
  geom_line(
    aes(
      x = time, 
      y = susceptible, 
      color = "susceptible"
    ), 
    linewidth = 0.5, 
    linetype = "dotted"
  ) + 
  geom_line(
    aes(
      x = time, 
      y = spreaders, 
      color = "spreaders"
    ), 
    linewidth = 1
  ) + 
  geom_line(
    aes(
      x = time, 
      y = non_spreaders, 
      color = "non_spreaders"
    ), 
    linewidth = 1
  ) + geom_line(
    aes(
      x = time, 
      y = fence, 
      color = "fence"
    ), 
    linewidth = 1
  ) + 
  scale_color_manual(
    values = 
      c(
        "spreaders" = "red", 
        "non_spreaders" = "blue", 
        "fence" = "grey", 
        "susceptible" = "black"
      ), 
    labels = 
      c(
        "spreaders" = "fans", 
        "non_spreaders" = "entrenched", 
        "fence" = "still considering", 
        "susceptible" = "never heard of her"
      )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 20), 
    breaks = seq(0, 20, 5)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 2000000),
    breaks = seq(0, 2000000, 200000)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Years", 
    y = "# people", 
    title = 
      str_wrap(
        "My intuition of what happens when a new attitude is dropped into an unexposed population", 
        75
        )
  ) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"), 
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
    legend.key = element_blank(), 
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom", 
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = "black"), 
    panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, color = "black")
  )
```
